request.spec:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All 4 Playwright tests now pass with `bin/e2e`.

**The requested behaviour already worked.** When I first ran the suite, the main "as of roles" test passed before I changed anything. Each time a sheet's today moves forward, the app saves a copy of the whole sheet, and roles are stored per sheet, so they're in that copy. With an as-of date set, the roles list is read from the right copy and shows the roles in force at the end of that day. I didn't change anything for roles.

**What was failing was the audit record for editing a person.** Scenario 3 failed on one line in the audit view:
- The test gives a person terms of 3 from a date, then saves them again with the terms field blank. The terms in force stay 3.
- The test expects that second save's line to end in `terms=3`, but the app wrote no `terms=` field at all.
- The cause: the app only checked whether the new value differed from the person's terms with no start date. Those were blank before and blank after, so it saw no change.

**The fix**, in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/Person.java` (`giveTerms`): a save now also counts as a terms change when the value entered differs from the terms in force. The old check is kept alongside it, so every line that recorded `terms=` before still does.

Side effect: a save like this one now adds `terms=<terms in force>` to the audit line even though the terms shown don't change. That is what the test expects, but it differs from before.
